title: Assembly of finitely many local quasi-compact atlases
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $Z$ be an $S$-scheme, let $A$ be an algebraic space over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], and fix $A\to h_Z$. Let $J$ be a finite set and let $(p_j:W_j\to Z)_{j\in J}$ be etale morphisms of schemes [def-weil-etale-morphism] whose images cover $Z$. For each $j$ let $U_j$ be a quasi-compact $S$-scheme [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme] and let $q_j:h_{U_j}\to A\times_ZW_j$ be a representable surjective etale morphism. Fibre products are sheaf fibre products [def-pc-fibre-product]. Then the induced morphism $$q:h_U\longrightarrow A,\qquad U=\coprod_{j\in J}U_j,$$ whose restriction to $U_j$ is $h_{U_j}\xrightarrow{q_j}A\times_ZW_j\to A$, is representable, surjective and etale. The scheme $U$ is quasi-compact. In particular $A$ admits a quasi-compact scheme atlas. The empty finite set $J$ is allowed when $Z$ is empty; no affineness hypothesis on $Z$ or $W_j$ is required.

source.place: Tag 03E3 (definition-quasi-compact) and Tag 040T (lemma-finite-disjoint-quasi-compact), scheme-atlas construction combined with topologies.tex Tag 0217 (lemma-etale), (2) and (3).

proof.text: Form the coproduct in schemes over S and transfer its colimit cocone to schemes using the colimit-preserving forgetful functor. Its inclusions are disjoint open immersions and cover. Their sieve is fppf covering since it is Zariski covering. The initial scheme has empty covering; any scheme mapping to two distinct summands is initial. Mathlib GrothendieckTopology.isColimitCofanMkYoneda therefore makes the represented coproduct a coproduct in fppf sheaves. Apply its descent and uniqueness operations to the composites a_j=q_j followed by the pullback projection. This constructs q and proves exactly the displayed restriction iff uniqueness assertion, including the empty family.

source.place: Tags 01JB/01JC; fppf sheaf gluing, with Mathlib Sites/Subcanonical.isColimitCofanMkYoneda.

proof.text: Use the scheme-source representability clause of representable_etale_scheme_tests for q. For each test t:h_T to A, obtain a representing pullback V with projections v:V to T and r:V to the coproduct U, using full faithfulness of Yoneda to recover r as a scheme map. The relative morphism-property API identifies the scheme-test definition of etaleness with the relative property of Etale on Over S. Since p_j is etale, the projection A times_Z W_j to A is representable etale by base change; composition with q_j proves every a_j representable etale.

source.place: Tag 025W and scheme-test properties preceding 025Y; Mathlib MorphismProperty.relative.

proof.text: Let D_j=V times_U U_j. Base-changing the Zariski cover of U by r gives an open cover of V. Pasting its represented pullback squares with the square defining V gives D_j as the test of a_j over t, with projection D_j to V to T. Step 2 makes each projection etale. Etaleness local on the source now proves v etale. No identification of V with a coproduct of new test schemes is needed.

source.place: Tag 02GJ; schemes.tex Tags 01JB/01JC after base change.

proof.text: Recover T to Z from t followed by a using Yoneda. Let B_j=T times_Z W_j. Their projections b_j to T form an etale cover. The two projections of B_j determine c_j:h_(B_j) to A times_Z W_j. Apply the surjectivity scheme test of q_j to c_j to obtain L_j to B_j surjective, together with a map h_(L_j) to h_(U_j). Its composite to h_U and its projection to h_T agree in A by the given restriction equation for q. The universal property of V and full faithfulness of Yoneda give L_j to V whose composite with v is L_j to B_j to T. Every point of T lifts to some B_j and then to L_j, so it lifts to V. This directly proves v surjective, without comparing D_j to L_j or invoking composition of covering families. The argument also handles empty J, since the base-changed cover then has no points to lift.

source.place: Tag 0217(3), followed by the pullback universal property and pointwise lifting.

proof.text: Steps 2-4 supply for every t a single representing square with projection both surjective and etale. These witnesses prove IsSurjective q and IsEtale q, while scheme-source representability gives IsRepresentable q. Transport the open cover of the scheme coproduct to the underlying scheme of the coproduct in Over S. Its index type is finite and each member is compact by hypothesis, so Scheme.OpenCover.compactSpace proves CompactSpace U. Return this compactness together with q and its uniqueness and scheme-test properties. No affineness assumption is used.

source.place: Tag 03E3; finite compact open-cover argument underlying Tag 040T.

proof_origin.place: Atlas construction in Tag 03E3, sheaf gluing via schemes.tex Tags 01JB/01JC, source-local etaleness via morphisms.tex Tag 02GJ, and pointwise lifting over topologies.tex Tag 0217(3). K6 formalization uses Mathlib sheaf coproduct and relative morphism-property APIs; it omits the original coproduct-distributivity and D_j/E_j comparison steps.

No new nodes and no statement changes. Checked all cited statements, empty index and empty-space cases, nonaffine and nonseparated bases.

tool_uses.why: Only the defining sheaf equalizer axiom is used to glue sections on disjoint Zariski pieces; this is a generic definition, not a different route.
Full Yoneda converts maps and natural isomorphisms of scheme representables into scheme morphisms and isomorphisms. The local-term unit supplies no replacement for this categorical tool.

Step 1: q is glued by the fppf sheaf axiom over the Zariski cover f^{-1}(U_j); overlaps are empty, and def-pc-fppf-site makes the empty family an fppf covering of the empty scheme, so A of the empty scheme is a singleton. Step 2: representable by the scheme-source clause of lem-trf-space-representable-etale-scheme-tests. Step 3: etale-covering-base-change and etale-covering-composition (singleton inner families) make the e_j : E_j -> T etale and jointly surjective. With the finite-coproduct base-change lemma (J finite) this gives V = coproduct of the E_j over T. Steps 5-6: locality on the source, surjectivity and finite subcovers are correct. Edge cases tested: empty J (forces Z empty and every test T empty), empty U_j, nonaffine or nonseparated data, and infinite J as a negative control. proof_deps equals the union of the step uses. lean.statement: theorem finite_qc_atlas_assembly {S : Scheme.{u}} (Z : Over S) (A : AlgebraicSpace S) (a : A.obj.obj ⟶ yoneda.obj Z) {J : Type v} [Finite J] (W : J → Over S) (p : ∀ j : J, W j ⟶ Z) (hp : ∀ j : J, Etale (p j).left) (hcover : ∀ z : Z.left, ∃ (j : J) (w : (W j).left), (p j).left w = z) (U : J → Over S) (hU : ∀ j : J, CompactSpace (U j).left) (qj : ∀ j : J, yoneda.obj (U j) ⟶ Limits.pullback a (yoneda.map (p j))) (hqjEt : ∀ j : J, IsEtale (qj j)) (hqjSurj : ∀ j : J, IsSurjective (qj j)) : CompactSpace (∐ U).left ∧ ∃ q : yoneda.obj (∐ U) ⟶ A.obj.obj, (∀ q' : yoneda.obj (∐ U) ⟶ A.obj.obj, (∀ j : J, yoneda.map (Sigma.ι U j) ≫ q' = qj j ≫ Limits.pullback.fst a (yoneda.map (p j))) ↔ q' = q) ∧ IsRepresentable q ∧ IsSurjective q ∧ IsEtale q
lean.note: The coproduct in Over S has underlying scheme the scheme coproduct, since Over.forget creates colimits. The atlas map is the unique map with the prescribed restrictions to the summands (iff form, so uniqueness does not depend on the atlas properties). Compactness and the three scheme-test properties give the stated quasi-compact scheme atlas; finite indices may be empty and live in an arbitrary universe.

reviewed_lean.note: H3: delivered `∃! q, restrictions ∧ IsRepresentable ∧ IsSurjective ∧ IsEtale` makes q unique only among maps with the atlas properties; the node's 'induced morphism' needs uniqueness from the restrictions alone (sheaf gluing, step 1). Fixed to iff form `∃ q, (∀ q', restrictions q' ↔ q' = q) ∧ Rep ∧ Surj ∧ Et`; fixes/SpaceFiniteQcAtlasAssembly.lean plus lean-record.json with the verbatim statement; nt_compile --json clean in 4.8 s. Everything else checked: Z, A, a : A→h_Z, finite J in universe v (empty allowed), Etale p_j, joint-cover hcover, CompactSpace U_j, q_j into pullback a (yoneda.map p_j) with scheme-test IsEtale/IsSurjective (representability included), ∐U in Over S equal to the scheme coproduct; dependency declarations (AlgebraicSpace.*, Mathlib Etale, CompactSpace, pullback) match their records; no extra hypotheses; sorry-only proof; source/blueprint docstrings; no new nodes; no citers in side-live.
